name: read
description: Read a file: numbered lines (`N<tab>text`), 2000 from `offset` (1-based) or `limit`; a cut result says how to continue. Images, PDFs (`pages`) and notebooks work too. Read before you edit; never copy the line-number prefix into an edit.

name: write
description: Create a file or replace one entirely. Overwriting needs a prior `read`; prefer `edit` for part of a file.

name: edit
description: Replace `old_string` with `new_string` in a file. It must occur exactly once (copy it from `read` without line numbers, with context to be unique), or set `replace_all`. `read` the file first.

name: multi_edit
description: Several `edit`s in one or more files, applied all together or not at all, in order (each sees the ones before it). `path` is the default file; an edit may name its own. An empty `old_string` creates a file. `read` each existing file first.

name: edit_lines
description: Edit lines by anchor. `read` shows each line as `N:hhh|text`; name a line by its anchor `N:hhh` (and the last line of a range by `end`). `op`: replace (default), insert_after, insert_before or delete. An anchor whose line changed since you read it is refused with fresh anchors. `anchor` "0" with insert_after writes at the top of the file.

end.description: Anchor of the last line of the range (default: `anchor`).

name: notebook_edit
description: Edit one cell of a Jupyter notebook (.ipynb). `cell` is the cell's id or 0-based index as `read` shows it. `mode`: replace (default) the cell's source, insert a new cell after `cell` (at the top without one), or delete it. `cell_type` sets the new cell's type and changes it on replace. Replacing a code cell clears its outputs. `read` the notebook first.
